A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TestNUC and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original content can be matched reliably; v2 adds Appendices D and E.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments across eight datasets, aggregation and embedding comparisons, scaling analyses, and prediction-stability measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds experiments with out-of-distribution contamination in Appendix D, Table 6.

M1.justification: Appendix E introduces TestNUC-S, which caches embeddings and previously generated predictions and reuses neighbor outputs to avoid repeated LLM calls. This adds a limited inference variant while retaining the original retrieval and voting procedure. Algorithm 1's added embedding-extraction line clarifies an existing operation.

E1.justification: Appendix D adds a distinct test scenario using BANKING data contaminated with 60% or 75% Reddit outliers. This extends coverage to out-of-distribution neighbor data; the original eight datasets and classification tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain Standard Prompting, Self-Consistency, KNN/TopK-ICL, KNN/TopK-ICL-P, Best-of-N, and Weighted Best-of-N. The new cost analysis uses previously evaluated baselines, and the contamination study compares existing voting variants. No baseline is added to or removed from a matched comparison.

E3.justification: The new contamination experiment varies OOD proportion, neighbor count, and naive versus weighted voting. Appendix E adds estimated per-sample runtime and monetary cost comparisons using GPT-4o-mini, including K=5, 10, and 50. The original evaluation settings, including 500 test examples per dataset, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds two substantive analysis areas absent from v1: robustness to heavily contaminated neighbor data and accuracy/runtime/cost tradeoffs, including cached inference. Tables 6 and 7 extend the evidence beyond the retained studies of data size, neighbor count, aggregation strategy, embedding model, and prediction stability.

E5.justification: Table 6 introduces ± uncertainty values for accuracy results, whereas v1's accuracy tables report point estimates. The meaning of these uncertainty terms and the associated repeat counts or seeds are unspecified. Appendix C's existing N=10 prediction-inconsistency protocol is retained.

E6.justification: Table 6 adds substantive contamination-dependent findings: under 75% OOD, weighted voting scores 74.0±0.5 at K=10 but falls to 59.0±0.7 at K=100, against 63.7±0.6 without neighbors. Table 7 adds runtime/cost estimates and cached-variant results. These extend findings on failure conditions and resource use; the original numerical results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The neighborhood-purity and voting definitions in Equations 1-3 are unchanged. The explicit embedding variables in Algorithm 1 restate existing computation, and Appendix E repeats existing complexity arguments. No new theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about neighboring unlabeled data, improvements across eight datasets, integration with existing inference methods, and scalability. Adding 'and Scaling' to the title emphasizes a claim already present in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix D extends the interpretation of similarity weighting to OOD contamination, arguing that unrelated neighbors receive lower weights. Appendix E explains the practical appeal of cached inference and its computational tradeoffs. The robustness discussion emphasizes gains without discussing the large-neighborhood failures shown in Table 6.

D1.justification: Appendix E documents what TestNUC-S stores and how cached embeddings and predictions are reused, and provides estimated per-sample runtime and dollar costs absent from v1. Existing sampling settings, embedding model, prompt instructions, and code-access information are retained. Cache construction costs are not separately quantified.

R1.justification: v2 adds supporting citations to Gu et al. (2025), Semi-supervised In-context Learning: A Baseline Study, and Wang et al. (2025), BANGS. The related-work sections and the paper's overall positioning relative to prior approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Edits include the expanded title, acknowledgements, removal of 'of FFA' from the prompt-template heading, an explicit embedding-extraction step, and two additional appendix sections. The main section order and most existing prose are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6 and 7, moves the unchanged Figure 7 upward on the final page, and reflows the appendices. Algorithm 1 becomes taller, and the NV-Embed-v2-7B scores in Table 4 gain bold emphasis. The original plots and numerical table contents are retained.

improvement.justification: The new contamination and cost analyses make v2 more informative about practical conditions and expose failure cases absent from v1, while preserving the original evidence. The benefit is limited by unspecified uncertainty and protocol details in Table 6, underdiscussed large-neighborhood failures, and estimated costs without separately quantified cache setup costs.
